texts.preamble: Anik Milk Products Private Limited vs Suresh Kumar Agarwal And Ors on 10 September, 2024 Ocdsl-1 Order
texts.facts: Considering the urgency and the prayer made by the counsel for the plaintiff, this Court has allowed the plaintiff to move the suit as unlisted motion. The plaintiff has prayed for leave under Clause 12 of the Letters Patent on the ground that the plaintiff is outside the jurisdiction of this Court but the defendant nos. 1 and 2 are within the jurisdiction of this Court. He submits the defendant no.3 is also outside the jurisdiction of this Court. Counsel for the plaintiff submits that some cause of action arose within the jurisdiction of this Court and some case of action arose outside the jurisdiction of this Court. This Court finds that sufficient cause has been shown for granting leave under Clause 12 of the Letters Patent. Accordingly, leave under Clause 12 of the Letters Patent is granted. The plaintiff has also prayed for leave under Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act and submitted that only in the last week of August and in the first week of September, 2024 the plaintiff came to know that the defendant is selling deceptively similar products of the plaintiff, namely, "Anik Ghee" and as such there is an urgency to file the an application and also to move an application praying for ad interim order. Accordingly, the plaintiff has not initiated pre institution mediation process. Accordingly, leave under Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act is granted. The plaintiff has also prayed for leave under Order II Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Plaint is admitted subject to scrutiny by the department. The plaintiff is allowed to move the application being GA- COM/1/2024 for ad interim order. The plaintiff has filed the present application for grant of ad interim order. In the year 2016 the plaintiff by way of deed of assignment obtained an irrevocable assignment and transfer, together with goodwill of certain trademarks from Anik Industries Limited for valuable consideration. In the year 1965 Hindustan Lever Limited adopted, coined and started using the mark 'ANIK' for selling various dairy products, including but not limited to ghee and milk in Class 29. The plaintiff has made extensive advertisement, marketing and the high quality of the ghee, the product under the mark "ANIK" bearing a unique and distinct get-up, packaging and colour combination which became extremely popular amongst the customers at large. Due to the continuous, extensive and uninterrupted use as well as the superior quality of the ghee products manufactured, marketed and sold under the mark "ANIK", the mark acquired goodwill and reputation amongst the customers across India, particularly, in North and East India. Anik Industries Limited also applied for registration for several "ANIK" trademarks over the years. The trademarks obtained by the Anik Industries Limited is still valid and subsisting. The plaintiff after obtaining the trademark applied to the Trademark Registry for getting its name 4 registered as a subsequent proprietor of the said trademarks. The mark Anik Milk Products Private Limited vs Suresh Kumar Agarwal And Ors on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169419171/ 3 "ANIK" along with a unique get-up, packaging, colour combination was continuously and extensively and uninterruptedly used by the plaintiff through its predecessor-in-title for the last more than five decades. In order to protect its customers from getting deceived and have health issues, the plaintiff employed and authorized dealers in parts of India for distributing and supplying the ghee products. By virtue of extensive, open, continuous and uninterrupted usage of the plaintiff's ghee product bearing the unique and distinct get-up, colour combination and packaging, trade dress under the trademark "ANIK" since 1965, the said mark has become inseparably and exclusively associated with the business identity of the plaintiff. The plaintiff's well-known trademark "ANIK" has become a prominent name in the dairy business which is used by the plaintiff as a house mark in respect of well-known and widely accepted products. Due to such prominence of the plaintiff's mark "ANIK" the ghee products bearing the trade dress has also achieved substantial goodwill, reputation and recognition in the market. For the year 2023-24, the total sale turnover of the plaintiff with respect of the Anik ghee is Rs.4,36,66,60,862/-.
texts.arguments: Counsel for the plaintiff submits that only when the plaintiff came to know that the defendant is selling the product which is deceptively similar to that of the plaintiff's product and accordingly, the plaintiff immediately filed the suit and there is chance of arising further cause of action in future and as such, leave is prayed for under Order II Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Learned counsel for the plaintiff submits that the defendant no.1 is carrying business under the name and style Sudha Ghee Deport and is engaged in the business of selling, marketing, distributing, offering to sell or dealing otherwise in spurious dairy product including ghee which are identical and deceptively similar and slavish copy of the products of the plaintiff bearing the trademark "ANIK" and the trade dress. He submits that 5 the defendant no.2 owns, runs, controls, manages and operates and interactive e-commerce website by the name of IndiaMART and the Anik Milk Products Private Limited vs Suresh Kumar Agarwal And Ors on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169419171/ 4 defendant no.2 runs, controls, manages and operates and interactive e- commerce Just Dial. Counsel for the plaintiff submits that the defendant nos. 1 to 4 appear to be firms/entities/persons inter alia engaged in the business of manufacturing, selling, marketing, distributing, offering to sell or dealing otherwise in spurious dairy products including the ghee which are identical and deceptively similar and slavish copy of the product of the plaintiff bearing trademark "ANIK" and the trade dress. He submits that in the last week of August 2024 the plaintiff came to know from its authorized distributors in Kolkata that the defendants are offering for sale, selling, manufacturing, marketing and otherwise dealing in spurious ghee products identical and deceptively similar trademark and trade dress of the plaintiff. He submits that on conducting further search on or about 29th August, 2024 and 2nd September, 2024 the plaintiff discovered that the defendants infiltrated the mark also through interactive e-commerce website i.e. IndiaMART and Just Dial with the misleading and contradictory information to deceive the customers into purchasing spurious inferior quality ghee products bearing the identical and deceptively similar trademark and the trade dress by giving an impression that those products somehow are connected or associated or originated by the plaintiff. Counsel for the plaintiff submits that the trademark "ANIK" and trade dress of the plaintiff are inherently a distinctive one and the 6 customers will assume that the spurious inferior quality ghee product bearing the identical and deceptively similar trademark and the trade dress Anik Milk Products Private Limited vs Suresh Kumar Agarwal And Ors on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169419171/ 5 of the defendant are either an offshoot of the plaintiff's mark or the defendants somehow are associated or connected with the plaintiff or its business. Counsel for the plaintiff submits that the act of infringement has been committed by the defendants as the defendants have purportedly used the plaintiff's trademark "ANIK" and trade dress in attempt to imitate authentic trademark/corporate name, domain name of the plaintiff with an intention to escape liabilities, if possible, in such a manner which has caused confusion and/or deception in the mind of public and the members of the trade as regards the source and origin of the goods. Counsel for the plaintiff submits that the defendants have no right to use the trademark "ANIK" and the trade dress in any manner whatsoever in respect of their spurious ghee products. He submits that the plaintiff has not permitted nor has granted any licence to the defendants to use the trademark "ANIK" and the trade dress or any other identical or deceptively similar mark and thus, the use of the same is clearly unauthorized, mala fide intention of the defendants to make illegal and wrongful gain from the immense goodwill and reputation gained by the plaintiff for the last more than five decades.
